title: Change of rings for presheaves of modules is left adjoint to restriction
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, let $a:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $X$, let $\mathcal M$ be a presheaf of $\mathcal A$-modules and $\mathcal N$ a presheaf of $\mathcal B$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Write $\operatorname{Res}_a\mathcal N$ for the presheaf $\mathcal N$ regarded as a presheaf of $\mathcal A$-modules, $\mathcal A(U)$ acting on $\mathcal N(U)$ through $a_U:\mathcal A(U)\to\mathcal B(U)$. Let $\mathcal B\otimes_{p,\mathcal A}\mathcal M$ be the presheaf $U\mapsto\mathcal B(U)\otimes_{\mathcal A(U)}\mathcal M(U)$ (with $\mathcal B(U)$ an $\mathcal A(U)$-module through $a_U$), whose restriction map along $V\subseteq U$ sends $b\otimes m$ to $b|_V\otimes m|_V$, made a presheaf of $\mathcal B$-modules by $\mathcal B(U)$ acting on the left factor. Then sending a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal B$-modules $v:\mathcal B\otimes_{p,\mathcal A}\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ to the family $(m\mapsto v_U(1\otimes m))_U$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal B\otimes_{p,\mathcal A}\mathcal M,\mathcal N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal M,\operatorname{Res}_a\mathcal N)$ onto the morphisms of presheaves of $\mathcal A$-modules, with inverse sending $w$ to the family $b\otimes m\mapsto b\,w_U(m)$; it is natural in $\mathcal M$ (a morphism $f:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M'$ acting on the left side by precomposition with $\mathrm{id}\otimes f$) and in $\mathcal N$.

proof.text: (The two presheaves.) Write $\rho^{\mathcal F}_{VU}$ for the restriction maps of a presheaf $\mathcal F$, $V\subseteq U$ open. Since $a$ is a morphism of presheaves of rings, $a_V(r|_V)=a_U(r)|_V$ for $r\in\mathcal A(U)$. (i) $\operatorname{Res}_a\mathcal N$ is a presheaf of $\mathcal A$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]: $(a_U(r)n)|_V=a_U(r)|_V\,n|_V=a_V(r|_V)\,n|_V$, so its restriction maps are semilinear over $\mathcal A(U)\to\mathcal A(V)$. (ii) $\mathcal B\otimes_{p,\mathcal A}\mathcal M$ is a presheaf of $\mathcal B$-modules: $\mathcal B(U)\otimes_{\mathcal A(U)}\mathcal M(U)$ is the base change of the $\mathcal A(U)$-module $\mathcal M(U)$ along $a_U$, a $\mathcal B(U)$-module by $b'(b\otimes m)=b'b\otimes m$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. For $V\subseteq U$ make $\mathcal B(V)\otimes_{\mathcal A(V)}\mathcal M(V)$ an $\mathcal A(U)$-module through $\mathcal A(U)\to\mathcal A(V)$; the map $\mathcal B(U)\times\mathcal M(U)\to\mathcal B(V)\otimes_{\mathcal A(V)}\mathcal M(V)$, $(b,m)\mapsto b|_V\otimes m|_V$, is biadditive and $\mathcal A(U)$-bilinear, since $(b\,a_U(r))|_V\otimes m|_V=b|_V\,a_V(r|_V)\otimes m|_V=r|_V\cdot(b|_V\otimes m|_V)$ and $b|_V\otimes(rm)|_V=b|_V\otimes r|_Vm|_V=r|_V\cdot(b|_V\otimes m|_V)$ (restriction of $\mathcal B$ is a ring map, that of $\mathcal M$ is semilinear). By the universal property of the tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] there is a unique additive (indeed $\mathcal A(U)$-linear) $\rho_{VU}$ with $\rho_{VU}(b\otimes m)=b|_V\otimes m|_V$. As the tensor product is generated by the elements $b\otimes m$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], the identities $\rho_{UU}=\mathrm{id}$, $\rho_{WV}\circ\rho_{VU}=\rho_{WU}$ ($W\subseteq V\subseteq U$) and $\rho_{VU}(b'x)=b'|_V\,\rho_{VU}(x)$ for $b'\in\mathcal B(U)$ hold because they hold on these generators ($(b'b)|_V\otimes m|_V=b'|_V(b|_V\otimes m|_V)$). So $\mathcal B\otimes_{p,\mathcal A}\mathcal M$ is a presheaf of abelian groups whose restriction maps are semilinear over $\mathcal B(U)\to\mathcal B(V)$, i.e. a presheaf of $\mathcal B$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification].

proof.text: (Open by open.) Fix an open $U$. Apply Algebra 05DQ [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-extension-hom] to the ring map $a_U:\mathcal A(U)\to\mathcal B(U)$, the $\mathcal A(U)$-module $\mathcal M(U)$ and the $\mathcal B(U)$-module $\mathcal N(U)$ (which, as an $\mathcal A(U)$-module through $a_U$, is $(\operatorname{Res}_a\mathcal N)(U)$): the map $\Phi_U:\psi\mapsto(m\mapsto\psi(1\otimes m))$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B(U)}(\mathcal B(U)\otimes_{\mathcal A(U)}\mathcal M(U),\mathcal N(U))\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A(U)}(\mathcal M(U),\mathcal N(U))$ with inverse $\Psi_U:\lambda\mapsto(b\otimes m\mapsto b\,\lambda(m))$, and for a $\mathcal B(U)$-linear $\beta:\mathcal N(U)\to\mathcal N'(U)$ one has $\Phi_U(\beta\circ\psi)=\beta\circ\Phi_U(\psi)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 05DQ (lemma-adjoint-tensor-restrict) and its proof (alpha'(m \otimes s)=s alpha(m), beta'(m)=beta(m \otimes 1)); invoked by the proof of Sheaves 006R

proof.text: (Compatibility with restrictions.) A morphism $v$ of presheaves of $\mathcal B$-modules is a family of $\mathcal B(U)$-linear $v_U$ with $v_V\circ\rho_{VU}=\rho^{\mathcal N}_{VU}\circ v_U$, and a morphism $w:\mathcal M\to\operatorname{Res}_a\mathcal N$ of presheaves of $\mathcal A$-modules is a family of $\mathcal A(U)$-linear $w_U$ commuting with restrictions [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. (a) If $v$ is a morphism, $w_U:=\Phi_U(v_U)$ commutes with restrictions: $w_V(m|_V)=v_V(1\otimes m|_V)=v_V(\rho_{VU}(1\otimes m))=v_U(1\otimes m)|_V=w_U(m)|_V$, using $1|_V=1$ and the formula for $\rho_{VU}$ of step 1. (b) If $w$ is a morphism, $v_U:=\Psi_U(w_U)$ commutes with restrictions: on a generator, $v_V(\rho_{VU}(b\otimes m))=v_V(b|_V\otimes m|_V)=b|_V\,w_V(m|_V)=b|_V\,w_U(m)|_V=(b\,w_U(m))|_V=\rho^{\mathcal N}_{VU}(v_U(b\otimes m))$, the fourth equality by semilinearity of the restriction of $\mathcal N$; both sides of $v_V\circ\rho_{VU}=\rho^{\mathcal N}_{VU}\circ v_U$ are additive and the elements $b\otimes m$ generate [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], so it holds. Hence $\Phi=(\Phi_U)_U$ sends $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal B\otimes_{p,\mathcal A}\mathcal M,\mathcal N)$ into $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal M,\operatorname{Res}_a\mathcal N)$ and $\Psi=(\Psi_U)_U$ goes back; they are mutually inverse because $\Phi_U$ and $\Psi_U$ are, for every $U$ (step 2). This is the bijection of the statement, with the stated formulas.

source.place: Tag 006R (lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict-presheaves), proof: 'This follows from the fact that for a ring map A -> B the restriction functor and the change of ring functor are adjoint' (the compatibility with restriction maps, left implicit there, written out)

proof.text: (Naturality.) For a morphism $f:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M'$ of presheaves of $\mathcal A$-modules, $\mathrm{id}\otimes f$ is the family $f_U\otimes_{\mathcal A(U)}\mathcal B(U)$ of $\mathcal B(U)$-linear maps $b\otimes m\mapsto b\otimes f_U(m)$ [def-weil-module-base-change]; it commutes with restrictions, as both composites send $b\otimes m$ to $b|_V\otimes f_V(m|_V)=b|_V\otimes f_U(m)|_V$ and these elements generate [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], so it is a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal B$-modules. For $v:\mathcal B\otimes_{p,\mathcal A}\mathcal M'\to\mathcal N$: $\Phi(v\circ(\mathrm{id}\otimes f))_U(m)=v_U(1\otimes f_U(m))=(\Phi(v)\circ f)_U(m)$, which is naturality in $\mathcal M$. For a morphism $\beta:\mathcal N\to\mathcal N'$ of presheaves of $\mathcal B$-modules (also a morphism $\operatorname{Res}_a\mathcal N\to\operatorname{Res}_a\mathcal N'$, since $\mathcal A(U)$ acts through $a_U$), $\Phi(\beta\circ v)_U=\beta_U\circ\Phi_U(v_U)$ by the naturality clause of step 2 [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-extension-hom], which is naturality in $\mathcal N$.

Step 2 is 05DQ at each U. Step 3 shows that the sectionwise bijections and their inverses carry morphisms of presheaves to morphisms of presheaves (compatibility with restrictions on generators b (x) m), so they assemble to the bijection with the stated formulas. Step 4 is naturality in M (id (x) f a morphism of presheaves, computed on 1 (x) m) and in N (the naturality clause of the leaf). No new node: every fact used is a Mathlib leaf or a definition node. No presheaf change-of-rings tensor node exists in the DAG (grep for 006R, otimes_{p, 'tensor product presheaf'; def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product is the sheaf tensor over one ring), so the construction stays inline in the statement as before. lean.statement: theorem changeOfRingsAdjunction : ∃ (T : PresheafOfModules.{max v w} R ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{max v w} S) (q : ∀ (M : PresheafOfModules.{max v w} R) (U : (TopologicalSpace.Opens X)ᵒᵖ), (ModuleCat.extendScalars (α.hom.app U).hom).obj (M.obj U) ≅ (T.obj M).obj U) (e : ∀ (M : PresheafOfModules.{max v w} R) (N : PresheafOfModules.{max v w} S), (T.obj M ⟶ N) ≃ (M ⟶ (restrictScalars a).obj N)), (∀ (M : PresheafOfModules.{max v w} R) (U V : (TopologicalSpace.Opens X)ᵒᵖ) (i : U ⟶ V) (b : B.presheaf.obj U) (m : M.obj U), (T.obj M).map i ((q M U).hom (b ⊗ₜ[A.presheaf.obj U,(α.hom.app U).hom] m)) = (q M V).hom ((B.presheaf.map i b) ⊗ₜ[A.presheaf.obj V,(α.hom.app V).hom] (M.map i m))) ∧ (∀ (M M' : PresheafOfModules.{max v w} R) (f : M ⟶ M') (U : (TopologicalSpace.Opens X)ᵒᵖ) (b : B.presheaf.obj U) (m : M.obj U), (T.map f).app U ((q M U).hom (b ⊗ₜ[A.presheaf.obj U,(α.hom.app U).hom] m)) = (q M' U).hom (b ⊗ₜ[A.presheaf.obj U,(α.hom.app U).hom] (f.app U m))) ∧ (∀ (M : PresheafOfModules.{max v w} R) (N : PresheafOfModules.{max v w} S) (f : T.obj M ⟶ N) (U : (TopologicalSpace.Opens X)ᵒᵖ) (m : M.obj U), (e M N f).app U m = f.app U ((q M U).hom ((1 : B.presheaf.obj U) ⊗ₜ[A.presheaf.obj U, (α.hom.app U).hom] m))) ∧ (∀ (M : PresheafOfModules.{max v w} R) (N : PresheafOfModules.{max v w} S) (g : M ⟶ (restrictScalars a).obj N) (U : (TopologicalSpace.Opens X)ᵒᵖ) (b : B.presheaf.obj U) (m : M.obj U), ((e M N).symm g).app U ((q M U).hom (b ⊗ₜ[A.presheaf.obj U,(α.hom.app U).hom] m)) = b • (show N.obj U from g.app U m)) ∧ (∀ (M M' : PresheafOfModules.{max v w} R) (N : PresheafOfModules.{max v w} S) (f : M ⟶ M') (h : T.obj M' ⟶ N), e M N (T.map f ≫ h) = f ≫ e M' N h) ∧ (∀ (M : PresheafOfModules.{max v w} R) (N N' : PresheafOfModules.{max v w} S) (β : N ⟶ N') (h : T.obj M ⟶ N), e M N' (h ≫ β) = e M N h ≫ (restrictScalars a).map β)
